title: The reference implementation's Exposure At Default accretes debt at the risk-free rate plus the borrow rate, which the specification does not describe
content:
A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.1.5.2 defines Exposure At Default in one sentence: "the total amount of funds from the Allocation System that have been deployed into the decentralized lending protocol." A present-tense balance.

The reference implementation computes something materially different:

`ead = sum(debt["debt_usd"] * math.exp((RISK_FREE_RATE + debt["borrow_apy_30d"]) * TIME_HORIZON) for ...)`

with `RISK_FREE_RATE = 0.04  # SOFR` declared as a module constant. This is a *forward* exposure — the debt grown continuously over the one-year horizon at the risk-free rate plus the position's 30-day trailing borrow APY. It is internally coherent, since PD is estimated over the same one-year horizon and the exposure at the moment of a future default is larger than today's, but it is not what the Atlas says.

The divergence has two distinct consequences. Substantively, capital requirements are higher than the prose implies, by roughly `exp((0.04 + borrow rate) × 1)` — a 10%+ uplift at plausible rates. Procedurally, a 4% SOFR assumption has entered the risk framework through committed code rather than through the Atlas, so it is not visible as a governed parameter and there is no stated process for updating it as rates move.

This is a general hazard of shipping a reference implementation alongside a normative specification: where they differ, the code silently wins, because it is what gets run — and undeclared constants inside it become de facto risk parameters.
description: Prose defines EAD as funds deployed into the protocol; the code computes debt × exp((0.04 + borrow APY) × T), introducing a 4% SOFR constant that appears nowhere in the Atlas text.
